title: Inverse Kinematics Chain Solver with Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive inverse kinematics (IK) chain solver with a physics debug overlay.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e). Perspective camera at position (0, 5, 15) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (5, 10, 5).
- A ground grid helper (size 20, divisions 20, color 0x333355) at y=0.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## IK Chain
- Create an IK chain of exactly 6 segments (bones). Each segment is a cylinder (radius 0.15, height 1.5) colored with a gradient from blue (0x2266ff) at the base to cyan (0x22ffcc) at the tip.
- The chain is anchored at a fixed base position (0, 0.75, 0). Each segment connects end-to-end via joints.
- Each joint has angular constraints: max bend angle of 45 degrees per joint.
- Implement a FABRIK (Forward And Backward Reaching Inverse Kinematics) solver that iterates up to 10 iterations per frame to converge.

## Target
- A glowing sphere (radius 0.4, emissive 0xff4444) that serves as the IK target.
- The target starts at position (3, 4, 0).
- The user can drag the target in 3D space using mouse (raycasting on a plane parallel to camera). When dragging, disable OrbitControls.
- A dashed line (0xff4444) connects the end effector (tip of last segment) to the target.

## Debug Overlay
- Toggle with the 'D' key. When enabled:
  - Draw small spheres (radius 0.1, color 0xffff00) at each joint position.
  - Draw colored arrows (AxesHelper-style, length 0.5) showing the local rotation axis at each joint.
  - Draw arc wireframes showing the angular constraint cone at each joint (yellow wireframe).
  - Display a line from each joint to the next showing the current bend angle as a color: green (0°) to red (45°).
- The debug overlay is OFF by default.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel (semi-transparent dark background) showing:
  - 'Segments: 6'
  - 'Iterations: {current_iterations}' (how many FABRIK iterations ran last frame)
  - 'End Effector Error: {distance_to_target}' (formatted to 4 decimal places)
  - 'Solver Converged: {true/false}' (converged if error < 0.01)
  - 'Debug: ON/OFF'
- A button labeled 'Reset Target' that moves the target back to (3, 4, 0).
- A button labeled 'Randomize Target' that moves the target to a random reachable position (within chain total length of 9 units from base, y > 0).
- A slider labeled 'Max Angle' (range 10 to 90, default 45) that adjusts the per-joint angular constraint in real-time.

## Physics / Solver Constraints
- Total chain reach = 6 segments * 1.5 = 9.0 units. If target is beyond reach, the chain should fully extend toward it.
- Joint angles must never exceed the configured max angle constraint.
- The base joint is fixed at (0, 0.75, 0) and must never move.
- The solver must be NaN-free; all joint positions must be finite numbers.
- End effector error must monotonically decrease (or stay same) across FABRIK iterations within a single frame.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- segmentCount: number (6)
- jointPositions: array of {x,y,z} for each joint (7 positions for 6 segments: base + 6 endpoints)
- targetPosition: {x,y,z}
- endEffectorPosition: {x,y,z}
- endEffectorError: number (distance from end effector to target)
- solverConverged: boolean
- solverIterations: number (iterations used last frame)
- debugOverlayVisible: boolean
- maxAngleConstraint: number (in degrees)
- jointAngles: array of 6 numbers (current bend angle in degrees at each joint)
- isDragging: boolean
- chainTotalLength: number (should be 9.0)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: FABRIK solver must respect per-joint angular constraints. Total chain length is 9.0 units. Base is fixed at (0, 0.75, 0). All joint positions must be finite (no NaN/Infinity). Joint angles must not exceed maxAngleConstraint. End effector error must decrease monotonically across solver iterations within a frame.
